audit_finding: AUDIT RESOLUTION (ISSUE 1): The apparent contradiction between Phase 6 and Phase 8 arose from an unsupported prose claim ('dropping liver plummets R2 to 0.0398, liver accounts for >90% of variance') that contradicted the actual on-disk experimental results. The verified on-disk metrics in exp6_xgboost_results.json and exp6_hsgin_results.json show: 1. Retrained Leave-One-Liver-Out R2 is 0.3758 for XGBoost (Delta = -0.0965) and 0.3914 for HSGIN (Delta = -0.1074). 2. Retrained Heart ONLY achieves R2 = 0.2232, Liver ONLY achieves R2 = 0.2083, Biomarker ONLY achieves R2 = 0.1531, and Kidney ONLY achieves R2 = 0.1492. 3. In Phase 8 held-out permutation attribution, Heart (29.8% share) and Liver (29.3% share) are the two primary drivers, with Biomarkers (21.6%) and Kidney (19.2%) providing substantial orthogonal signal. 4. Both Phase 6 and Phase 8 consistently demonstrate that FIB-4 prediction in the leakage-controlled setting is a genuinely multi-organ task: Liver markers provide hepatic injury tone, Heart features (BPXOSY1) provide the primary surrogate proxy for patient age, and Biomarkers (LBXWBCSI) provide the surrogate proxy for platelet count.
